ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, point B lies on the hyperbolic function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ (where $k<0$, $x<0$), and point A lies on the negative half of the x-axis. Connect points A and B, and rotate the line segment AB $90^\circ$ counterclockwise around point A. The corresponding point to B after the rotation is point C. Suppose point C also lies on the graph of the hyperbolic function $y=\frac{k}{x}$. Given that the y-coordinates of points B and C are 4 and 1 respectively, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As illustrated, draw BM perpendicular to the x-axis at point M through point B; draw CN perpendicular to the x-axis at point N through point C. \\
Hence, $BM=4$, $CN=1$, $\angle AMB=\angle CNA=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAM+\angle ABM=90^\circ$, \\
Due to the property of rotation: $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $AB=CA$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAM+\angle CAN=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABM=\angle CAN$,\\
In $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle CAN$, we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle AMB=\angle CNA=90^\circ \\ \angle ABM=\angle CAN \\ AB=CA \end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABM\cong \triangle CAN(AAS)$, \\
$\therefore BM=AN=4$, $AM=CN=1$, \\
Let $OA=a(a>0)$, hence $OM=OA-AM=a-1$, $ON=AN+OA=4+a$, \\
$\therefore B(1-a, 4)$, $C(-4-a, 1)$, \\
Substituting points $B(1-a, 4)$, $C(-4-a, 1)$ into the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ yields: $4(1-a)=k=-4-a$, \\
Solving, we get $a=\frac{8}{3}$, \\
Thus, $k=-4-a=-4-\frac{8}{3}=\boxed{-\frac{20}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, and A is located on the negative half-axis of the x-axis; the curve is a branch of an inverse proportional function located in the second quadrant. Point B is on the curve, located above A and still on the left side of the y-axis; point C is also on the curve, located to the left of A and slightly above the x-axis. After line segment AB is rotated counterclockwise 90° around A, it corresponds to AC. Reasoning: According to the coordinate/vector rotation method, let A=(-t,0), where t>0. Let B=(x_B,4), because the y-coordinate of B given in the problem is 4. Vector AB=(x_B+t,4). When rotating counterclockwise 90° around A, vector (u,v) becomes (-v,u), so the rotated vector is (-4,x_B+t). Therefore C=A+(-4,x_B+t)=(-t-4,x_B+t). The problem gives the y-coordinate of C as 1, so x_B+t=1, that is x_B=1-t, hence C=(-t-4,1). Because B and C are both on the same inverse proportional function y=k/x, their xy products are both equal to k: k=4(1-t)=1(-t-4). Solve the equation 4(1-t)=-t-4, obtaining 4-4t=-t-4, 8=3t, t=8/3. Therefore k=4(1-8/3)=4(-5/3)=-20/3.
